title: Sebastian and the Oath
premise: Quentin Dravenmoor, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden her magic for ten years in the city of Vellmark, where speaking an oath aloud can bend reality—and where magic is punishable by fire. When crown inquisitor Sebastian Corvane arrives to hunt the gifted, he unknowingly rents a room from her, and their uneasy friendship becomes the story's central betrayal. Quentin discovers the hunt is a cover for the crown's plan to harvest dragon-fire and forge an unbreakable army, which would reignite the ancient war her order died to end. In the end, Quentin must break her own sacred oath—speaking truth instead of binding silence—to shatter the crown's ritual, sacrificing her power and exposing herself, while Sebastian chooses loyalty to her over the throne that made him.
about_author: Cyrus Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath rituals before turning to fantasy. They write in a drafty tower room and insist all their characters deserve better than they get.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Quentin's POV. Quentin sells a luck-charm to a frightened dockworker, revealing her careful double life and the vow of silence that binds her swordspeaking gift. When she hears rumor of a royal edict against magic, fear sharpens into resolve: stay invisible at any cost. Emotional beat: the exhausting loneliness of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: A Room for the Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Crown inquisitor Sebastian Corvane arrives in Vellmark and, needing discretion, rents her spare room. Quentin recognizes his badge instantly but cannot refuse without suspicion. Their first conversations are fencing matches of politeness. Emotional beat: dread braided with an unexpected, unwelcome flicker of kinship—two people both performing versions of themselves.

chapters.title: What the Ash Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian investigates a burned apothecary, hunting traces of the gifted, and finds a scorched oath-sigil he doesn't report. Flashbacks reveal he owes the crown a debt from a family scandal. He begins suspecting Vellmark hides something larger than petty charm-sellers. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt as he realizes his superiors want more than arrests.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin's old mentor's dying message reaches her: the crown is gathering dragon-fire, the last living flame, to fuel a ritual of bound obedience. If it succeeds, every mind in the realm bends to the throne. She must decide whether to act or run. Emotional beat: terror giving way to the first stirrings of responsibility—the oath she swore may demand more than silence.

chapters.title: Knives Over Cards
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A raid on the night market forces Quentin to use a whisper of her gift to save a child, witnessed by Sebastian, who covers for her without saying why. Trust deepens even as betrayal becomes inevitable for them both. Emotional beat: intimacy built on complicity—each now holds a secret that could destroy the other.

chapters.title: The Confession Neither Spoke
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts Quentin indirectly, laying out evidence over dinner, and she confesses everything: last swordspeaker, the mentor's warning, the dragon-fire plot. Instead of arresting her, he asks how to stop it. Emotional beat: relief and vertigo—the moment loyalty shifts from institution to person, making them traitors together.

chapters.title: Where Loyalties Are Weighed
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The pair infiltrate the citadel's undercroft and find the dragon-fire caged and dying, its keeper a broken former swordspeaker Quentin thought dead. The keeper warns the ritual needs an oath-bound voice as its final component—her. Emotional beat: horror and grief, as Quentin learns her survival was never accidental; she has been bait all along.

chapters.title: The Trap Wears a Friendly Face
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The crown anticipated Sebastian's turn; his handler reveals they've used him as a leash on Quentin all along, threatening his family. Ordered to deliver her, he must choose. He burns his warrant and warns her, knowing there is no way back. Emotional beat: the cost of choice—Sebastian severs his old identity and accepts ruin.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the ritual, Quentin does the unthinkable: she breaks her binding oath by speaking a new one aloud—truth wielded as a weapon—that unravels the ceremony and frees the dragon-fire back into the world. The backlash strips her gift forever. Sebastian holds the line against guards who were once his brothers-in-arms. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation; victory purchased with the self she was.

chapters.title: Embers Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue-like. Months later, magic is still feared but no longer hunted wholesale; small lights reappear in Vellmark's alleys. Powerless Quentin opens a real shop, no charms required, while Sebastian—disgraced but free—sweeps her step each morning. The last dragon-fire glimmers on the horizon, alive. Emotional beat: quiet peace earned through loss; identity rebuilt not around power, but truth.
